deckTitle: Laboratory Medicine Wrestling: The Numerical Noir & The Biomarker Betrayal

cards.power: The Water-Warp. Pulls Water-Tokens whenever he goes. The high Sodium is a Mimic: whatever it does with fluid, Osmolality has already noted it.
cards.lore: The Osmotic-Anchor. Fixing Hypo-Nats too fast = Osmotic-Demyelination Syndrome (aka Kayfaboggle).
cards.gradeReason: Volume lord owns the ring name AND the move — hydration danger is immediate and visceral.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Epic graphic novel. Subject: Armored sea-titan commanding surging tidal waves. Mood: Commanding, elemental.

cards.power: The Voltage-Trigger. Controls the Resting-Heart of heart wires. Off Balance? The Heart gets confused.
cards.lore: Hyper-K-the-Killer creates Peaked-T-Wave-Mountains. Hypo-K-Nail opens the Valley. Beware of Error.
cards.gradeReason: Spark-Plug name fires instantly — every player knows what a spark plug does to an engine.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Electro-comic. Subject: Lightning serpent coiling around a twitching human heart. Mood: Volatile, dangerous.

cards.power: The Membrane-Stabilizer. Keeps Nerve-Gates steady. Hypo-Cal = Gates Slamming, Hyper-Cal = Gates shut.
cards.lore: Regulated by Parathyroid-Hormone. If Mag-the-Magnet is low, Calcium won't rise.
cards.gradeReason: Concrete stabilizer works but asks why concrete — the membrane gate metaphor needs a moment to click.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Stone-etched illustration. Subject: Gargoyle holding iron nerve-gates closed with both hands. Mood: Solid, imposing.

cards.power: The Gatekeeper's-Helper. The Universal-Relaxer holding the Potassium/Calcium gates shut.
cards.lore: Low Mag triggers Torsade-de-Told. The Ignored-Electrolyte causing Mystery-Glitches.
cards.gradeReason: Magnet is evocative but gatekeeper-helper role is secondary — needs the Potassium/Calcium context to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Psychedelic lab art. Subject: Octopus wrapped around ion channels, tentacles holding gates. Mood: Hidden, powerful.

cards.power: The Oxygen-Tank. Determines available Breath-Fuel. Dark color = low Hemoglobin = fainting from Cargo-Penalty.
cards.lore: The Cargo-Ship. Without Iron-Bolts, the ship can't carry oxygen-crates.
cards.gradeReason: Cargo ship with oxygen-crates is a perfect vessel metaphor — load it and sail, no explanation needed.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Steam-age illustration. Subject: Donkey loaded with glowing oxygen canisters crossing mountains. Mood: Hardworking, essential.

cards.power: The Hole-Sealer. First-Responders to a Leak-Crisis. Low count (Thrombo-the-Thin) = bleeding from scratches.
cards.lore: Too high = Clot-the-Blocker. Beware-HIT-the-Hunter is in the ICU!
cards.gradeReason: Hole-Sealer is the clearest single-function name in the deck — you know the job before the text.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cartoon emergency response. Subject: Beaver-platelet slapping a dam patch over a hemorrhage. Mood: Urgent, heroic.

cards.power: The Riot-Scanner. High (Leuko-the-High) = Infection-Incursion. A Left-Shift shows massive Peaked-Battalions deployed or Intranuclear-Rookie (bands).
cards.lore: Neutrophils fight bacteria. Eosinophils fight Parasite-Punks and Allergy-Killjoys.
cards.gradeReason: War-count opens the role but four sub-cell types dilute the single-move clarity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Military briefing art. Subject: Army ant battalion launching from a radar screen. Mood: Mobilized, tactical.

cards.power: The Cell-Architect. Tells the Detective if Red-Cells are big (Macro-Mix) or small (Micro-Misfit).
cards.lore: Micro-Mitch = Iron-Deficiency. Macro-Max = B12 or Folate-Famine.
cards.gradeReason: Size-gage describes the tool not the move — detective framing helps but is one remove from performance.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Detective noir illustration. Subject: Owl with magnifying glass comparing giant and tiny red blood cells. Mood: Analytical, precise.

cards.power: The Filter-Score. The Trash-Count in the blood. Rising score = Kidney-Filters are clogged/failing.
cards.lore: A late indicator. If Kidney-Gears have already seized up, Creatinine is already mixed up.
cards.gradeReason: Waste-marker is descriptive; filter-score does more work but the late-indicator caveat muddies the role.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Industrial cartoon. Subject: Raccoon hauling overflowing trash cans past clogged kidney filters. Mood: Grimy, urgent.

cards.power: The Dehydration-Signal. When ratio > 20, shows the wrestler is Fluid-Starved.
cards.lore: Rises when thirsty, or if Hank-Builder is hiding in the GI tract (Protein-loading).
cards.gradeReason: Messenger is passive — dehydration signal carries more urgency but the BUN/Creatinine ratio math dampens immediacy.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Desert Western. Subject: Camel messenger trudging through cracked desert carrying a water gauge. Mood: Parched, weary.

cards.power: The Clearance-Clock. How fast the body can Flush-the-Toxins and clear-the-Mold.
cards.lore: Calculated from Area/Age/Gender. If GFR < 15, it's Dialysis-Time.
cards.gradeReason: Clearance-Clock plus Dialysis-Time threshold — you know exactly when the match is lost.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Hourglass fantasy. Subject: Glowing hourglass emptying through golden kidney-shaped filters. Mood: Measured, critical.

cards.power: The Precise-Scan. For wrestlers too Sarcopenic-Thin or Bodybuilder-Buff for a standard Area-check.
cards.lore: A stable Trash-Marker produced constantly by all nucleated cells.
cards.gradeReason: Pure-filter describes a lab property — who plays Cystatin-C at the table? No one knows what to do.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Clean lab tech. Subject: Musclebound biochemist holding a crystalline filter above kidney cross-section. Mood: Sterile, precise.

cards.power: The Cell-Burst-Signal. High ALT = Liver-Cells are smashing their Chemical-Guts into the bloodstream.
cards.lore: The Liver-Sentry. Thousands of units = something Catastrophic from Toxic-Assault or Viral-Vandalism.
cards.gradeReason: Cell-burst-signal is vivid — chemical guts spilling out is unforgettable. Immediately actionable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Toxic grunge. Subject: Green factory building exploding, chemical barrels spilling into a river. Mood: Catastrophic, leaking.

cards.power: The Multi-Damage-Marker. Less specific than ALT. If AST is much higher than ALT, think Al-the-Alcoholic-Wrecking-Blow.
cards.lore: Also spikes in Heart-Hall and Muscle-Meltdown rhapsody.
cards.gradeReason: Misfit captures the non-specificity beautifully but multi-damage-marker needs ALT comparison to mean anything.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Battered wrestler illustration. Subject: Bulldog referee wearing liver, heart, and muscle badges simultaneously. Mood: Confused, bruised.

cards.power: The Chronic-Status-Bar. Built by the liver; a low score means the Factory-is-Broken or falling for weeks.
cards.lore: Low Albumin causes Edema-the-Swelling because the Water-Magnet is gone.
cards.gradeReason: Pressure-magnet is accurate physics but the Chronic-Status-Bar framing takes two beats to land.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Slow decay illustration. Subject: Giant magnet slowly losing its charge, water flooding in around it. Mood: Gradual, ominous.

cards.power: The Jaundice-Flow. High indicates the hamster-wheels are exploding. Bilirubin-cells are absolutely yellow-tinted.
cards.lore: The Waste-Product of hemoglobin. High Direct Bili means clogged Bile-Grime-and-Bile-Spool.
cards.gradeReason: Jaundice-flow is vivid but Direct-vs-Indirect split asks players to read the subtext before acting.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Toxic spill art. Subject: Chameleon dripping yellow bile from overflowing green pipes. Mood: Saturated, jaundiced.

cards.power: The Refusal-Toolkit. The Gold-Standard proof that Cardio-Cell-Membranes are actively dying.
cards.lore: The Molecular-Skeleton. If it's in the blood, the cell membrane has been fatally breached.
cards.gradeReason: Heart-Scream may be the deck's best name — players feel the emergency before reading a word.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Anatomical horror. Subject: Screaming anatomical heart with membrane cracks leaking gold light. Mood: Visceral, urgent.

cards.power: The Flood-Warning. When heart-walls Stretch from too much fluid, BNP yells at kidneys to Dump-the-Water.
cards.lore: Differentiates Lung-Mist-Pneumonia from Heart-Failure-Flood.
cards.gradeReason: Flood-warning with Dump-the-Water command — there's a move and a consequence built into one line.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Cartoon flood emergency. Subject: Bloated tomato-frog shouting at kidneys while water pours over heart walls. Mood: Panicked, swollen.

cards.power: The Time-Witness. Disappears fast. Used to see if the wrestler is having a second heart attack right after the first.
cards.lore: Troponin stays high for days. CK-MB is the Short-Term-Witness.
cards.gradeReason: Re-Infarct-Finder is an active job title — the time-witness metaphor gives it a unique role no other card occupies.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Crime scene noir. Subject: Cheetah stopwatch detective examining a second heart injury timeline. Mood: Rapid, forensic.

cards.power: The Clot-Rule-Out. Low D-Dimer = NO clot. High means something is breaking down (Infection, Trauma, or Clot).
cards.lore: The Scraps of a Fibrin clot. It is a Screen, never a Diagnosis.
cards.gradeReason: Clot-Rule-Out is precise and clinically useful but Debris implies aftermath not action.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Forensic illustration. Subject: Magnifying glass over shredded fibrin rope fragments in bloodstream. Mood: Investigative, cautious.

cards.power: The Thin-Check. Warfarin High-the-Old-Guard. High INR = High Bleed-Risk.
cards.lore: Liver failure raises INR because the sick liver can't build Factor-V-the-Key.
cards.gradeReason: Tracker is passive — Thin-Check activates the card but Warfarin context is required for most players.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Armadillo coil illustration. Subject: Armored armadillo with blood-thinning gauge strapped to shell. Mood: Cautious, precise.

cards.power: The Speed-Limit. Monitors Heparin-the-Gravy. Too high = bleed note like Water-Iguana.
cards.lore: Measures the Intrinsic-and-Common-Highways.
cards.gradeReason: Hitch is an odd word for this biomarker — speed-limit metaphor works but the name doesn't invite a move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Speed-limit road art. Subject: Snake coiled around an hourglass with a red warning gauge. Mood: Tense, monitored.

cards.power: The Resource-Count. Without it, Platelet-Plugs can't stick. In DIC-the-Disaster, the supply is Consumed to zero.
cards.lore: The vital Raw-Material for the Fibrin-Mesh.
cards.gradeReason: Glue-Supply is both role and stakes — DIC consuming it to zero makes the loss catastrophic and immediate.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Resource management art. Subject: Giant glue factory being drained by a vortex labeled DIC. Mood: Depletion, crisis.

cards.power: The X-Ray-Vision. Tracks Factor-X-Inhibitors when standard PT/aPTT are completely blind to them.
cards.lore: Used in Obese-Wrestlers or Renal-Fail-Days to verify dose safety.
cards.gradeReason: Modern-Monitor is a description not an invitation — X-Ray-Vision saves it but the card name still explains, not performs.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: X-ray surveillance. Subject: Hawk with X-ray goggles tracking invisible clot-busting molecules in bloodstream. Mood: Vigilant, technical.

cards.power: The Feedback-Loop. High TSH = Brain screaming at a Sleepy-Then-Thyroid. Low TSH = Thyroid is Over-Driven.
cards.lore: The Pituitary-Sentry is always watching.
cards.gradeReason: Brain screaming at a sleepy thyroid is one of the deck's most embodiable images — players feel the hierarchy instantly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Command hierarchy art. Subject: Bulldog general shouting orders at a sleeping butterfly thyroid. Mood: Authoritative, frustrated.

cards.power: The Cheat-Detector. Reveals Average-Sugar-State over 90 days. You can't fake a Fling-From-Diets from Average-Sugar-State.
cards.lore: Binds itself to the Red-Cell-Inventory for its full 120-day lifespan.
cards.gradeReason: Cheat-Detector is this deck's headline card — the 90-day memory makes lying to your doctor impossible. Hall of fame.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Detective memory palace. Subject: Elephant detective reading a 90-day sugar calendar stamped on red blood cells. Mood: Relentless, knowing.

cards.power: The Survival-Fuel. Zero = Addison-the-Crash (Shock). Too high = Cushing-the-Corb (Obesity/Thin skin).
cards.lore: Fight-or-Flight. Caveat: High ICU stress artificially spikes this stat.
cards.gradeReason: Stress-stat describes the function; Addison and Cushing named examples add substance but require context.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dual nature illustration. Subject: Squirrel split between raging fire (high) and collapsed floor (zero). Mood: Volatile, survival.

cards.power: The Origin-Finder. Proves if blood insulin was Home-Made (Pancreas) or Injected (Syringe).
cards.lore: Type 1 Diabetics have ZERO C-Peptide. Insulinoma-Ian has massive amounts.
cards.gradeReason: Twin framing is clever but Origin-Finder is the active move — takes one beat to explain why twins matter.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Twin detective art. Subject: Two monkey scientists, one natural and one injected, side by side in matching suits. Mood: Investigative, revealing.

cards.power: The Living-Truth. Tells exactly how well Lung-Balloons exchange air and if blood is going Acid or Base.
cards.lore: Normal pH = Balanced Bella. Low pH + High pCO2 = Lung-over-Lazy (Respiratory Acidosis).
cards.gradeReason: Living-Truth is aspirational but ABG interpretation is complex — Bella does too much in one card.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Balancing act art. Subject: Flamingo balanced on pH scale between acid and base bubbles. Mood: Delicate, precise.

cards.power: The Starvation-Counter. High Lactate = Cell-Engines are starving for oxygen. Burning Emergency-Fuel.
cards.lore: High Lactate = Sepsis-Alert. The body is burning without oxygen at the cellular engine level.
cards.gradeReason: Oxygen-debt is a classic concept that clicks, but Emergency-Fuel burning is slightly repetitive as role-signal.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Industrial catastrophe. Subject: Furnace burning without oxygen supply, cells collapsing around it. Mood: Desperate, starving.

cards.power: The Mystery-Acid-Finder. High Gap = a Hidden-Acid-Saboteur is in the blood (Ketoacids, Lactic, Toxins).
cards.lore: MUDPILES. The Gap tells you precisely what kind of acid is ruining the match.
cards.gradeReason: Mystery-Acid-Finder plus MUDPILES mnemonic — this card is a complete clinical move with instant table utility.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Mystery thriller. Subject: Badger detective finding hidden acid vials labeled MUDPILES in a blood canal. Mood: Investigative, urgent.

cards.power: The Silent-Suffocator. CO hitches a ride on the Red-Cell-Inventory, permanently blocking oxygen from boarding.
cards.lore: The Cherry-Red wrestler. The standard hGy-Sensor is totally fooled into thinking blood is 100% oxygenated.
cards.gradeReason: Silent-Suffocator plus Cherry-Red detail plus pulse-ox blind-spot — three visceral facts that make the card unforgettable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Stealth horror. Subject: Carbon monoxide ghost smuggled inside red blood cell, blocking oxygen at the door. Mood: Invisible, lethal.

cards.power: The Fire-Alarm. Rises fast during Bam-Sepsis or a Joint-Riot. Confirms the Battle is Active.
cards.lore: An Acute-Phase-Reactant. Doesn't say where the fire is, just that the Immune-Army is mobilising.
cards.gradeReason: Fire-Alarm is immediate — you hear it, you move. The limitation (no location) is baked into the lore perfectly.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Emergency response art. Subject: Meerkat pulling fire alarm while immune army soldiers mobilize in background. Mood: Alarmed, fast.

cards.power: The Slow-Burn-Tracker. Spikes in chronic Auto-Immune-Wars like Lupus-Larry. The Old-School-Inflammation-Clock.
cards.lore: Inflammation makes red cells stick together and Sink-Fast in a test tube.
cards.gradeReason: Slow-burn is accurate and evocative but Sed-Rate is insider shorthand — players outside medicine need the POWER text.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Old clockwork. Subject: Tortoise referee with a test tube watching red cells sink slowly in amber liquid. Mood: Slow, methodical.

cards.power: The Antibiotic-Cue. High = Bacterial-Punks are present. Low = it's just a Viral-Rascal.
cards.lore: The ultimate weapon to help the team stop Antibiotic-Overuse.
cards.gradeReason: Bacteria-Beacon plus Antibiotic-Cue — the clinical action (prescribe or withhold antibiotics) is crystal clear.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Sci-fi beacon art. Subject: Jedi-green lighthouse specifically lighting up bacterial organisms, ignoring viral shadows. Mood: Precise, decisive.

cards.power: The Positive-Identification. Tells the team the exact Name-and-Weapon of the bacteria in the Blood-Highway.
cards.lore: Sterile-Technique is vital. If Skin-Steward-Staph gets into the bottle, it's a False-Alarm.
cards.gradeReason: Clan-Finder is evocative but Positive-Identification does the heavy lifting — sterile technique caveat adds needed complexity.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Bloodhound detective. Subject: Basset hound sniffing two blood culture bottles at crime scene table. Mood: Methodical, revealing.

cards.power: The Giant-Guard. High PSA = Prostate-Towers are inflamed (Prostatitis) or under siege by Malignant-Max.
cards.lore: Not 100% specific. A massive BPH-Benign-Giant also raises the score.
cards.gradeReason: Prostate-Picket implies a border sentinel but multiple causes muddy the signal — a picket can be friendly or hostile.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Castle siege art. Subject: Knight standing guard at prostate tower with both benign and malignant invaders outside. Mood: Ambiguous, watchful.

cards.power: The Recurrence-Radar. Not for finding cancer initially, but watching if it returns after the Blade-Brigade removes it.
cards.lore: A rise after surgery = the Shadow-Malignancy is creeping back.
cards.gradeReason: Recurrence-Radar is sharp clinical framing but Monitor is passive — it watches, it doesn't move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Surveillance radar. Subject: Owl monitoring radar screen watching for cancer shadow returning after surgery. Mood: Vigilant, post-op.

cards.power: The Peritoneal-Patrol. A Follow-up tool. Also triggers for Endo-Ball and Fibroid-Fiona.
cards.lore: Any physical irritation of the peritoneal lining can artificially raise this above normal.
cards.gradeReason: Ovarian-Alert and Peritoneal-Patrol are vivid but the multiple false-positive triggers make the role ambiguous.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Security patrol art. Subject: Alarm light above ovary scanning peritoneal space with multiple false-alarm signals. Mood: Alert, uncertain.

cards.power: The Mass-Classifier. If Liver-the-Livy has a lump + high AFP, it's likely Malignant-Max.
cards.lore: Dual-use: Also the marker for Fetal-Neural-Tube-Leaks in the Gyn-field.
cards.gradeReason: Tumor-Track is clear in the liver context but dual fetal use makes players hesitate at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Mass detection art. Subject: Angry wolf sniffing liver lump while fetal neural tube glows in background. Mood: Threatening, dual-natured.

cards.power: The Quick-Urine-Scan. Reveals a Bladder-Riot (UTI). Sugar-Leak = Diabetes exploiting the Filter-Overflow.
cards.lore: Nitrite + Leukocyte = Bacteria-the-Punks are absolutely present.
cards.gradeReason: Bladder-Riot is immediately performative — players role-play the UTI scenario before the lore ends.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Color-strip lab art. Subject: Lemur holding rainbow dipstick above a urine sample like a treasure map. Mood: Quick, diagnostic.

cards.power: The Diabetic-Kidney-Sentinel. Finds the Tiny-Protein-Leaks long before the standard dipstick can see them.
cards.lore: The very first clinical sign of Diabetic-Nephropathy.
cards.gradeReason: Early-Warning plus Sentinel watching for tiny leaks the dipstick misses — clinical urgency baked into the name.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Early detection art. Subject: Hawk spotting microscopic protein droplets leaking from kidney before disaster. Mood: Watchful, preventive.

cards.power: The Hidden-Bleed-Finder. Locates Invisible-Hank-the-Haemorrhage in the gut (early sign of Carci-Cure-All).
cards.lore: Only detects human blood. No Red-Meat-Interference to cause false alarms.
cards.gradeReason: Fecal-Occult is memorable but unappetizing as a table role — Hidden-Bleed-Finder does the performative lift.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Hidden clue illustration. Subject: Raccoon detective finding invisible blood drops in colon tunnel with UV flashlight. Mood: Covert, essential.

cards.power: The Brain-Bunker-Report. Differentiates Bacterial-Mist (low sugar, high protein) from Viral-Vandalism (normal sugar).
cards.lore: Drawing the sacred liquor of the soul to check the inner sanctum.
cards.gradeReason: Brain-Bunker-Report with Bacterial vs Viral split — the lore adds gravitas and the move is crystalline.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Sacred map illustration. Subject: Lumbar puncture needle drawing glowing spinal fluid from a fortified brain vault. Mood: Sacred, decisive.

cards.power: The Toxic-Cloud. If Liver-the-Limp fails, Ammonia builds up and triggers Encephalopathy-GI-Confusion/Coma.
cards.lore: The chemical culprit behind Asterixis (the Flapping Hand-Tremor).
cards.gradeReason: Brain-Fog Toxic-Cloud plus Flapping Hand-Tremor — three visceral images that make liver failure instantly embodiable.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Toxic fog illustration. Subject: Green ammonia cloud engulfing a confused brain while hands flap uncontrollably below. Mood: Toxic, confusing.

cards.power: The AutoDigestion-Alarm. When Lipase is >3x normal, the Pancreas-Factory is literally Eating-Itself.
cards.lore: The definitive hallmark of Acute Pancreatitis.
cards.gradeReason: Pancreas-Puncture plus AutoDigestion eating itself — visceral self-destruction is the most memorable image in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Body horror illustration. Subject: Pancreas factory melting its own walls while alarm bells ring and enzymes leak. Mood: Catastrophic, auto-destructive.

cards.power: The Crystal-Slayer. High levels precipitate into Needles that ruthlessly stab the joints and the Kidney-Filters.
cards.lore: The painful end-product of Purine metabolism.
cards.gradeReason: Crystal-Slayer plus Needles stabbing joints — no explanation needed, pain is physically embodied in the card name.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Crystal combat. Subject: Porcupine made of uric acid crystals launching needle spines into a swollen joint. Mood: Sharp, painful.

cards.power: The Inventory-Check. Proves if the Iron-Bolts are truly fasting (Anemia-Ansia) or just hidden away.
cards.lore: Caveat: During a Systemic-Riot, the body locks the Iron in the vault. Ferritin will look Falsely-High.
cards.gradeReason: Iron-Vault is poetic but the Falsely-High caveat during inflammation creates a move that can backfire at the table.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Fantasy vault art. Subject: Iron strongbox inside inflamed body glowing false signals during systemic chaos. Mood: Deceptive, hidden.

cards.power: The Cardiac-Gamble. Level > 2.0 = Dig-Tox-Ian appears, causing Yellow-Vision and heart blocks.
cards.lore: Hypokalemia makes the heart wires Hyper-Sensitive to Digoxin's poison.
cards.gradeReason: Narrow-Window as card name is a perfect pharmacology metaphor — the danger of crossing the line is felt immediately.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Tightrope danger art. Subject: Fox balancing on a narrow ledge above a toxic cardiac chasm with yellow fog. Mood: Precarious, dangerous.

cards.power: The Liver-Destiny. Predicts if the wrestler survives the overdose or if the liver-Factory is mathematically doomed.
cards.lore: Treatment relies entirely on the N-Acetyl-Cysteine-Rescue.
cards.gradeReason: Liver-Destiny is powerful but Nomogram in the card name is pure technobabble — it explains the tool, not the stakes.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Fate graph art. Subject: Rumack-Matthew graph as a battle map with liver-destiny plotted above the danger line. Mood: Mathematical, fateful.

cards.power: The Mind-Stabilizer. Too low = Barry-Bipolar swings. Too high = The-Shakes-and-Tremors + Renal-Failure.
cards.lore: Competes directly with Sodium in the Kidney-Filters.
cards.gradeReason: Mind-Stabilizer is the right role but Salt-Level is generic — the sodium competition lore is the real insight buried in text.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Anchor stability art. Subject: Anchor with a sodium/lithium balance scale keeping manic waves and depressive depths at bay. Mood: Stabilizing, narrow.

cards.power: The CNS-Depressor. Decodes why the wrestler is unconscious. Is it The-Drink-Or-Metabolic (Ketoacidosis)?
cards.lore: Cleared at an absolute, unchangeable constant rate of 15-20 mg/dL per hour.
cards.gradeReason: Ethano-the-Al-Level is a clever wordplay but CNS-Depressor framing is clinical not performative — zero-order kinetics is the gold.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Zero-order chemistry art. Subject: Bottle labeled CNS-Off emptying at a steady metronomic rate into a sinking wrestler. Mood: Steady, depressing.

cards.power: The Data-Validator.
cards.lore: The patient is the test; the lab is the subtext. Trust the numbers, but always verify the clinical fit. Stay fluffy!
cards.gradeReason: Meta-card that wraps the deck — QC Master role is clear but Data-Validator is thin as a power move.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Quality control laboratory. Subject: FrizzleBob rabbit in lab coat inspecting data sheets at quality control station. Mood: Authoritative, whimsical.

cards.lore: A wrestler with Renal-Ray-Failure is found with a heart rate of 50. The ECG shows massive Peaked-Mountains.
cards.gradeReason: Quest format demands immediate play — identify Hyper-K and execute Calcium-the-Shield. Pure performative scenario.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Quest scroll art. Subject: ECG strip shaped as mountain peaks above a failing kidney and slowing heart. Mood: Urgent, clinical.

cards.lore: A diabetic wrestler arrives unconscious. Bella says pH is 7.0, and the Anion-Gap is exactly 25.
cards.gradeReason: DKA scenario with exact numbers — players must chain Anion-Gap + Ketoacids + Missing-Gap into one diagnosis.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Acid emergency art. Subject: Unconscious wrestler surrounded by ketone clouds and a pH meter reading 7.0. Mood: Acidic, critical.

cards.lore: Wrestler has yellow skin, dark urine, pale stools. Lab reveals High-Direct-Bilirubin and High-Lipase.
cards.gradeReason: Yellow skin + blocked pipe + pancreatitis chain — three cards fire simultaneously. Best multi-synthesis in the deck.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Plumbing disaster art. Subject: Yellow-tinged wrestler with blocked bile pipe and exploding pancreas factory next door. Mood: Obstructed, cascading.

verdict: Uncle FrizzleBob's clinical lab deck runs 56 cards covering the full diagnostic alphabet from Sodium to Ethanol, and the wrestling metaphor holds remarkably across all of them. Name engineering like Troponin-the-Heart-Scream, HbA1c-the-Three-Month-Memory, and Anion-Gap-the-Missing-Acid is hall-of-fame material. The Synthesis Quest cards on page 15 are a structural masterstroke — forcing players to chain four or five cards into one live clinical scenario. Weak spots: the ABG and Lactate lore get repetitive, and Cystatin-C and Anti-Xa still read like textbook entries not wrestling moves. Table-ready: Y.
blurb: The complete wrestle-ready lab manual for med students and educators. 56 cards covering electrolytes, CBC, kidney panels, coagulation, hormones, tumor markers, and toxicology — every biomarker given a job title and a reason to fight.

coverQA.coverVisual: 4 — FrizzleBob rabbit in lab coat with beakers, dramatic noir lighting, strong composition
coverQA.coverTitle: 5 — The Numerical Noir & The Biomarker Betrayal is an excellent noir subtitle with real flair
coverQA.coverVibeMatch: 5 — Wrestling + medicine + detective noir aesthetic expressed perfectly in one frame
coverQA.coverOriginality: 4 — Strong original concept; fewer visual clichés than most medical education covers
coverQA.coverViral: 4 — Medical education niche will stop scrolling for this cover immediately
coverQA.coverNote: One of the stronger MedKayfab covers — the noir framing elevates what could have been a boring lab manual cover. The FrizzleBob rabbit anchors the brand while the beakers and dramatic lighting signal serious educational depth. Could push to 5 with a single Peaked-Mountain ECG trace in the background.

notes: 15 pages: 1 cover + 13 card pages (4 cards each = 52 cards) + 1 final page (Doc FrizzleBob QC card + 3 Synthesis Quest scenario cards = 4 cards) = 56 total. Card numbering runs 1-56 continuously. Synthesis Quest cards (54-56) use LORE-only format with a QUEST field instead of POWER — unique structure not seen in other decks. No RAF dice boxes visible. Artwork is highly consistent across all 56 cards — pen-and-ink with watercolor wash, matching throughout. MedKayfab MegaPack subfolder contains multiple decks; this is the Laboratory Medicine edition. ABG lore text (card 29) appears slightly garbled in source — simplified here.
